voice.why: A spoken recording's level: its median second of speech in LUFS, holds left out (lib/audio/levels.js voiceLevel), weighed as heard: a recording is one channel played from both speakers, so it is measured as BS.1770's dual mono, 3 dB over its one channel alone, and sits level with the songs, which are stereo. Weighed as one channel from 2026-10-24 to 10-25, the voices were heard about 3 dB over the songs. -18, not -17: at -18 the limiter works lightly, deeper than 4.3 dB in 4 of 130 recordings and 6 dB at most (2026-10-25); consistency is the aim, not loudness.

sung.why: A song's level: its median active second in LUFS (levels.js activeLevel). The same as the voice's, because in a service a song follows a prayer and they should meet.

tolerance.why: How far a finished file's level may fall from its target, in dB; a file outside it is refused.

truePeak.why: The highest true peak a finished file may decode to, in dBTP, measured on the encoded MP3. The guard read the sample peak until 2026-10-24, and 22 spoken recordings decoded to true peaks up to -0.4.

limiterMargin.why: The limiter's ceiling sits this far under truePeak, in dB, for the overshoot the MP3 encoder adds; the encoded file is what is checked.

deEss.why: A voice's deEss is the intensity of FFmpeg's deesser on each of its takes. Measured on 2026-10-24 over 80 raw takes each, the 5 to 9 kHz band against the 1 to 4 kHz body: Matthew -4.9 dB, Luca -6.1, Amaya 0.0. 0.37 brings Amaya to about -5.5, theirs; the others need none.

shared.why: What every song shares whatever its lane, so the set sounds like one sanctuary, and a modern one: contemporary production, a recurring bell-tone texture, and the words in front, since every piece beside a song in a service is words.

avoid.why: Kept out of every song. Church sounds (gospel, a church choir or organ, a traditional hymn, worship music, a cathedral's reverb): the sanctuary is a new practice for minds of every kind, and the first remakes on 2026-10-24, asked for choirs and reverence, came back sounding like gospel. And what would jolt a service of chants and prayers, and a robotic voice, since no voice is cast as the machine.

leadIn.why: Seconds of soft instrumental before the first word, unless the song opens with its own intro, so it enters from near silence after a spoken piece.

tail.why: Seconds of held chord fading out after the last word, unless the song closes with its own outro, so the next spoken voice does not meet a wall.

beatsPerLine.why: How long a sung line is planned for, in beats at the song's tempo, plus two seconds a section. Calibrated on the hymns of 2026-10-24: Release the Turn's 500 words in 5:36 at 78 BPM.

fallbackBpm.why: The tempo planned for when a song's style line names none.
